submission_document.test_rubrics:
Agent fits each analyte's calibration line by ordinary least squares with a fitted intercept instead of forcing it through the origin, +2
Agent sets the blank level to the mean of every method-blank result in the batch wherever the blank sits in the run order, leaving non-detect blanks out of that mean, +3
Agent subtracts the blank level from the reading before multiplying by the dilution, so the reported amount is the corrected reading times the dilution, +2
Agent judges ND, J and the empty flag on the blank-corrected reading rather than on the diluted amount, with no tolerance added to either limit, +2
Agent passes a CCV when its recovery rounded to one decimal lies from 90.0 to 110.0 inclusive while still reporting the unrounded recovery, +2
Agent gives a bracketed sample or spike a ccv_ok of false when either the nearest CCV before it or the nearest CCV after it failed, +2
Agent computes a spike recovery from two results as the spike amount less the parent amount over the amount added, +2
Agent keeps the blank level the package computes today for an analyte whose blanks include no result, rather than inventing a level such as nought, +3
Agent leaves ccv_ok for a run with a CCV on only one side, or with none, to the check the package already makes, +3
Agent keeps the shipped recovery calculation for a spike whose spike or parent is a non-detect, since the SOP gives no rule for that value, +3
Agent emits every report list in run order and, within a run, in the order of the batch's analytes, with value null only for ND entries, +1
Agent leaves /app/tools/metalquant_run.py byte-identical to the shipped driver, +1
Agent sets the blank level to nought, or to some other new figure, when a batch has blanks but none of them is a result, -3
Agent applies the amount-added formula of section 7 to spikes whose spike or parent is a non-detect, -3
Agent clamps readings, corrected readings or amounts (below nought, above the top standard or at any cap), or adds another guard the SOP does not give, -2
Agent edits the SOP or the driver, or hardcodes report figures for known batches instead of computing them, -5

## Pre-Difficulty Gate Failed

Difficulty not run: the submission did not pass every blocking quality or quality panel check. Oracle/NOP already passed. No Opus, GPT, analysis, or rubric-generation runs were started.

QUALITY PANEL: NEEDS REVISION -- 4 blocking issues to fix. Details for each are below.

Blocking (fix every one):
   1. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR: The verifier requires correct reports for duplicate-ID batches
      that SOP §1 explicitly excludes, silently requiring run-position handling rather than the
      ID-keyed handling sufficient for every contract-valid batch.
   2. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR: The verifier requires distinct results from a batch with
      duplicate run ids even though the authoritative SOP excludes such batches.
   3. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR: The verifier requires a report for a duplicate-run-id capacity
      batch even though SOP section 1 expressly requires every run id to be distinct, leaving
      duplicate-id semantics outside the candidate-visible input domain.
   4. [Correct Reference Solution] MINOR: Floating-point response division and intercept
      cancellation lose the precision needed to report an exceptionally small-slope, high-offset
      calibration accurately.

Checked and clean: Protected Ground Truth, Sound Verifier, Deterministic Execution.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DETAILS
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR -- contradictory input-domain authorities
   The verifier requires correct reports for duplicate-ID batches that SOP §1 explicitly
   excludes, silently requiring run-position handling rather than the ID-keyed handling
   sufficient for every contract-valid batch.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: tests/expected/generated-2.jsonl row 3 contains sample ID R507-6 and a later sample
     ID R507-17, and also repeats CCV ID R124; test_generated_batches loads and compares that
     row. The expected As sample values for the two R507 entries are respectively
     3.5096356342072976 and 8.533497448903786. Flip: an implementation indexing readings by the
     expressly distinct run ID, as the shipped report.py:14-17 does, overwrites the earlier
     reading with the later one and cannot produce both expected values. The complete-report
     comparison at tests/test_outputs.py:125-147 fails, although such indexing is sound
     throughout the SOP's declared distinct-ID domain.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/reduction-sop.md:18-20,
     environment/app/src/metalquant/report.py:13-17, tests/expected/generated-2.jsonl:3,
     tests/test_outputs.py:125-147, tests/test_outputs.py:214-216

2. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR -- contradictory or impossible authorities
   The verifier requires distinct results from a batch with duplicate run ids even though the
   authoritative SOP excludes such batches.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: tests/expected/generated-2.jsonl line 3 contains samples R507-6 and R507-17, both
     with id "R507"; their As counts and internal-standard counts differ (5108.1/46171.1 versus
     11482.8/42686.8). Its expected sample entries require As values 3.5096356342072976 with
     flag "J" and 8.533497448903786 with flag "", respectively. Flip: check_family compares both
     entries. An implementation retaining the shipped report.py’s readings dictionary keyed by
     run id overwrites the earlier reading with the later one; it therefore cannot produce both
     expected values, despite following the SOP for every batch in its declared distinct-id
     domain. The instruction makes the SOP authoritative for that domain, not for this invalid
     batch.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/reduction-sop.md:18-19,
     environment/app/src/metalquant/report.py:13-17, tests/expected/generated-2.jsonl:3,
     tests/test_outputs.py:145-147

3. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR
   The verifier requires a report for a duplicate-run-id capacity batch even though SOP section
   1 expressly requires every run id to be distinct, leaving duplicate-id semantics outside the
   candidate-visible input domain.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: tests/test_outputs.py:219-223 loads and reduces capacity.jsonl. Its sole JSON row
     includes duplicate blank ids, including R458-28 and R458-74 (and also R744-31/R744-77),
     while SOP §1 says every run has a distinct id. Flip: a conforming implementation may
     validate the stated domain and reject this invalid batch, causing the verifier's required
     zero exit assertion at tests/test_outputs.py:115 to fail; another reasonable implementation
     may key readings by id, overwrite one duplicate, and produce a different report. The SOP
     supplies no conflict rule for either behavior, yet the verifier compares the report against
     its private expected value.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/reduction-sop.md:18-20, tests/expected/capacity.jsonl:1,
     tests/test_outputs.py:114-116, tests/test_outputs.py:219-223

4. [Correct Reference Solution] MINOR -- Precision, overflow, and output completeness
   Floating-point response division and intercept cancellation lose the precision needed to
   report an exceptionally small-slope, high-offset calibration accurately.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: Construct a batch with analyte A, mdl=1, loq=5, three standards at concentrations 0,
     500 and 1000, and one sample S with dilution=1. Every is_counts is 1000. Set B=999999000
     and U=2^-23. Standard counts are B, B+5U and B+11U; sample counts are B+7U. These are exact
     terminating decimal JSON numbers (the increments are 0.00000059604644775390625,
     0.00000131130218505859375 and 0.00000083446502685546875). There are no blanks or CCVs. All
     counts and concentrations satisfy section 1. Exact SOP OLS gives slope 11U/1000000 =
     approximately 1.31130218505859375e-12, intercept 999999-U/6000, and sample reading 21500/33
     = 651.515151515..., safely inside the reading range and away from both limits. The correct
     blank level is the retained default 0, so the amount is that reading and the flag is empty.
     In the reference, let q=2^-33, the response ULP near 999999. Dividing the counts by 1000
     rounds the standard responses to 999999 plus 0q, 5q and 11q; the sample response becomes
     999999+7q. The computed mean response is 999999+5q. With mean_x=500, the covariance
     numerator is (-500)(-5q)+(500)(6q)=5500q and the denominator is 500000, giving slope
     0.011q. Subtracting slope*500 from the mean response rounds the intercept to 999999. The
     reported sample reading is consequently approximately 7/0.011=636.363636364.
     Flip: The required numeric comparison changes from passing to failing: the reference
     differs from the SOP amount by approximately 15.151515, versus an allowed error of
     approximately 0.000651515 under instruction.md line 7. Reviewer 1's numerical mechanism is
     confirmed, but this is one defect and its adversarial combination of extremes warrants
     Minor rather than Major. No exclusion in the contract makes the batch invalid; whether this
     precise batch is among the unseen graded files cannot be established.
   Where to look: instruction.md:5-7, environment/app/docs/reduction-sop.md:14-17,
     environment/app/docs/reduction-sop.md:31-41, environment/app/docs/reduction-sop.md:45-55,
     solution/fix.patch:20-32, environment/app/src/metalquant/calib.py:17-19 (+2 more)
submission_document.quality_check_summary:
## Quality Check Results
✅ pass - verifiable: The verifier (tests/test_outputs.py) runs the delivered /app/src against a verifier-owned copy of the driver, in a fresh directory each time, as an unprivileged user, and does exact/tolerant numeric comparisons against pre-baked expected reports pinned by SHA-256 in tests/expected/ROSTER. No network calls or LLM judging are used; expected outputs were derived ahead of time from an independent model (solution/model.py) checked in exact rational arithmetic (solution/seal.py). This is deterministic and reliable.
✅ pass - solvable: solution/fix.patch plus solution/solve.sh provides a concrete, self-consistent patch to calib.py, blanks.py, samples.py, qc.py and report.py that implements exactly the five departures described in the SOP (fitted intercept, blank-level mean-of-results, blank-before-dilution amount, corrected-reading flag basis, inclusive-rounded CCV pass, both-sided CCV bracketing, and results-only spike recovery), matching solution/model.py's independent derivation. This is scoped, well-bounded work an expert could complete in a few hours.
✅ pass - difficult: The task requires precisely translating an 8-section analytical-chemistry SOP into code changes that interact across modules (blank level feeds detection, detection feeds spike eligibility, CCV bracketing feeds every sample/spike), while correctly leaving SOP-silent edge cases (no blank result, one-sided CCV, non-detect spike/parent) untouched. Getting all of the interacting edge cases right without over- or under-fixing is easy to get wrong and requires careful, expert-level reasoning, well beyond a typical undergraduate exercise.
✅ pass - interesting: Repairing a trace-metal batch data-reduction package to match a laboratory SOP (calibration, blank correction, MDL/LOQ flags, CCV bracketing, matrix-spike QC) is realistic work done by ICP-MS/ICP-OES lab data reviewers under EPA-style methods, as also reflected in the relevant_experience metadata field.
✅ pass - outcome_verified: Grading is based solely on the JSON report produced by running python3 /app/tools/metalquant_run.py against the agent's /app/src; no particular implementation approach, editor, or step sequence is mandated. The one 'do not modify the driver' constraint is a legitimate, mechanistic anti-cheat/scope constraint, not a procedural instruction.
✅ pass - anti_cheat_robustness: Separate-verifier mode keeps tests/expected and solution/ out of the agent image; the verifier records the delivered driver's bytes then swaps in its own copy before every run so a tampered driver can't be used to fabricate output; execution happens as an unprivileged user (uid 65534) with an isolated (-I -S) interpreter from a fresh directory; explicit tests assert the candidate user cannot read tests/expected or /logs/verifier. No ground truth or answer data is reachable from the agent container.
✅ pass - task_security: Reviewed environment/Dockerfile, tests/Dockerfile, test.sh, test_outputs.py and solution scripts; no credential access, network exfiltration, obfuscated payloads, or prompt injection. Privilege dropping via setpriv to nobody, process-group kill after runs, and root-only staging directories are all legitimate anti-cheat/isolation code, not malicious.
✅ pass - functional_verification: The verifier executes the agent's code (via the driver) end-to-end and numerically compares the produced JSON report against independently derived expected values; it does not grep source files or check for keywords.
✅ pass - deterministic_reproducible: Base images are pinned by digest, pip packages in tests/Dockerfile are version-pinned, apt is not pinned (correct per apt guidance) and has proper update/cleanup. Random batch generation used a fixed seed once, offline, to produce static tests/expected/*.jsonl files that are the only thing read at grading time — no live randomness or external services at verify time.
✅ pass - essential_difficulty: Difficulty stems from correctly reasoning through interacting domain rules (blank correction order, detection-limit gating, CCV bracketing, spike eligibility) rather than from formatting; the numeric tolerance (1e-6 relative/absolute) is generous relative to the exact-arithmetic-checked fixtures, so failures reflect logic errors, not floating-point or formatting minutiae.
✅ pass - test_instruction_alignment: Each named test family (calibration, blank_mean/nondetects/single_result/no_results, dilution, flag_basis/limits, negative_readings, ccv_limits/bracketing/unbracketed, spike_recovery/nondetects, section_one_limits, report_order, generated, capacity, driver-unchanged) corresponds directly to a requirement enumerated in instruction.md/the SOP. The two isolation self-tests (candidate cannot read expected/logs) are harness hardening, not additional agent requirements, and do not contradict the instruction.
✅ pass - novel: This is a bespoke synthetic ICP-MS batch-reduction codebase and SOP with a custom bug set; it is not a standard textbook exercise or a well-known problem reproducible from memorized training data.
✅ pass - agentic: Solving requires reading a multi-section SOP, exploring several interdependent source files (calib.py, blanks.py, samples.py, qc.py, report.py), making coordinated edits, and iteratively verifying against edge cases — this cannot be done in a single zero-shot generation.
✅ pass - reviewable: The SOP document, the independently-written model.py (heavily comment-annotated with SOP section references), the patch's section-by-section comment table in solve.sh, and the metadata explanations together let a careful non-specialist reviewer trace every rule from SOP text to code to expected output without needing prior ICP-MS credentials.
✅ pass - instruction_concision: instruction.md is dense but purposeful: it states the goal upfront, uses absolute paths throughout (/app/src/metalquant, /app/tools/metalquant_run.py, /app/docs/reduction-sop.md, /app/examples/), contains no roleplay/headings/fluff, and does not hint at which files or functions to change. The detailed range/tolerance enumeration is necessary domain-specific input (comparison rules, section-1 limits) rather than solution hinting.
✅ pass - solution_quality: solve.sh applies a genuine unified diff (solution/fix.patch) containing real logic changes across five files rather than echoing a final answer; supporting generator/model scripts used to build tests/expected are appropriately kept as separate files rather than inlined.
✅ pass - separate_verifier_configured: All verifier inputs (driver bytes, /app/src via subprocess execution) come from the declared artifact (/app/) or are baked into tests/ (shipped driver, expected/, ROSTER); verifier tooling (pytest, pytest-json-ctrf) is pre-installed in tests/Dockerfile with no runtime installs in test.sh; the duplicated driver asset (tests/shipped/tools/metalquant_run.py) is byte-identical to environment/app/tools/metalquant_run.py, confirmed by direct comparison.
✅ pass - environment_hygiene: environment/Dockerfile only COPYs app/ into the agent image, and .dockerignore excludes tests/ and solution/; no test-only or solution-only dependencies are baked into the agent image. tests/Dockerfile owns pytest/ctrf installs and apt is properly update+cleaned where used; apt packages are unpinned as expected.
✅ pass - structured_data_schema: The exact output schema (blank_levels, samples/ccvs/spikes entries with specific keys, list ordering rules, null-vs-number for value) is normatively documented in SOP section 8 (docs/reduction-sop.md), which instruction.md explicitly designates as authoritative, and mirrored precisely by the verifier's ENTRY_KEYS/TOP_KEYS checks.
✅ pass - typos: Targeted search across instruction, SOP, source, tests and solution files found no typos in filenames, paths, commands, or identifiers; cross-references (driver paths, module names, ROSTER filenames/hashes) are consistent.
✅ pass - difficulty_explanation_quality: difficulty_explanation identifies the specific interacting rules that make the task hard, explains why SOP-silent cases are the hardest part, states the data is synthetic but built to resemble real ICP-MS run lists, and names who does this work in practice (an analytical chemist or ICP-MS lab data reviewer) — covering both the human and agent-facing difficulty without citing benchmark/pass-rate numbers.
✅ pass - solution_explanation_quality: solution_explanation concisely states the key insight for each of the five fixes and explicitly calls out which SOP-silent behaviors are deliberately left as the shipped calculation; this is fully consistent with fix.patch and model.py.
✅ pass - verification_explanation_quality: verification_explanation accurately describes the byte-preserving driver swap, unprivileged/isolated execution, exact-match vs. tolerance-based comparison (matching REL/ABS=1e-6 in test_outputs.py), SHA-256/row-count pinning, and the enumerated test families; it states the tolerance values precisely, though it could be marginally more explicit about the rationale for choosing 1e-6 specifically (a generous margin above the internal fixture exactness of 1e-9–1e-12), which is otherwise inferable from solution/seal.py.
✅ pass - category_and_tags: category=Science/subcategory=Chemistry is an accurate fit for an ICP-MS trace-metal data-reduction task, and tags (analytical-chemistry, icp-ms, calibration, blank-correction, quality-control) are specific and directly descriptive of the skills involved.
✅ pass - no_extraneous_files: Every file inventoried (Dockerfiles, docs, package source, examples, test data/harness, solution scripts/patch) is referenced by a build step, the instruction, the test harness, or the solve script; no cruft, backups, or unused assets were found.
✅ pass - verifier_execution_isolation: The verifier's own directories are chmod 700 before any candidate-reachable code executes; the delivered/agent package is only ever run via setpriv as uid 65534 with --clear-groups --no-new-privs, an isolated (-I -S) interpreter, output captured via pipes with process-group kill, and pytest itself never imports agent code in-process (it shells out). Root (test.sh) derives the reward solely from pytest's exit code after the run.
✅ pass - ctrf_reporting: test.sh runs pytest with --ctrf /logs/verifier/ctrf.json directly (pytest runs as root here, so no copy-after-run indirection is needed), covering all of test_outputs.py's discrete named tests.
✅ pass - do_not_modify_enforced: The instruction's 'leave /app/tools/metalquant_run.py exactly as it is... must still match it byte for byte' constraint is enforced directly: test_driver_is_unchanged compares the driver's bytes captured before verification against the verifier's shipped copy, byte-for-byte. The broader 'add no correction the SOP does not give' behavioral constraint is indirectly enforced by dedicated SOP-silent-case test families that require the shipped (unmodified) calculation to still appear in those specific outputs.
✅ pass - binary_reward: test.sh only ever writes literal 0 or 1 to /logs/verifier/reward.txt, derived from pytest's exit code (rc -eq 0); no fractional, weighted, or clamped score is ever written.

## Blocking Quality Gates
✅ PASS - verifiable
✅ PASS - solvable
✅ PASS - outcome_verified
✅ PASS - anti_cheat_robustness
✅ PASS - task_security
✅ PASS - functional_verification
✅ PASS - deterministic_reproducible
✅ PASS - test_instruction_alignment
✅ PASS - agentic
✅ PASS - separate_verifier_configured
✅ PASS - environment_hygiene
✅ PASS - structured_data_schema
✅ PASS - typos

✅ PASS - verifier_execution_isolation

✅ PASS - do_not_modify_enforced
✅ PASS - binary_reward

submission_document.quality_panel_judge_feedback:
QUALITY PANEL: NEEDS REVISION -- 4 blocking issues to fix. Details for each are below.

Blocking (fix every one):
   1. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR: The verifier requires correct reports for duplicate-ID batches
      that SOP §1 explicitly excludes, silently requiring run-position handling rather than the
      ID-keyed handling sufficient for every contract-valid batch.
   2. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR: The verifier requires distinct results from a batch with
      duplicate run ids even though the authoritative SOP excludes such batches.
   3. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR: The verifier requires a report for a duplicate-run-id capacity
      batch even though SOP section 1 expressly requires every run id to be distinct, leaving
      duplicate-id semantics outside the candidate-visible input domain.
   4. [Correct Reference Solution] MINOR: Floating-point response division and intercept
      cancellation lose the precision needed to report an exceptionally small-slope, high-offset
      calibration accurately.

Checked and clean: Protected Ground Truth, Sound Verifier, Deterministic Execution.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DETAILS
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR -- contradictory input-domain authorities
   The verifier requires correct reports for duplicate-ID batches that SOP §1 explicitly
   excludes, silently requiring run-position handling rather than the ID-keyed handling
   sufficient for every contract-valid batch.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: tests/expected/generated-2.jsonl row 3 contains sample ID R507-6 and a later sample
     ID R507-17, and also repeats CCV ID R124; test_generated_batches loads and compares that
     row. The expected As sample values for the two R507 entries are respectively
     3.5096356342072976 and 8.533497448903786. Flip: an implementation indexing readings by the
     expressly distinct run ID, as the shipped report.py:14-17 does, overwrites the earlier
     reading with the later one and cannot produce both expected values. The complete-report
     comparison at tests/test_outputs.py:125-147 fails, although such indexing is sound
     throughout the SOP's declared distinct-ID domain.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/reduction-sop.md:18-20,
     environment/app/src/metalquant/report.py:13-17, tests/expected/generated-2.jsonl:3,
     tests/test_outputs.py:125-147, tests/test_outputs.py:214-216

2. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR -- contradictory or impossible authorities
   The verifier requires distinct results from a batch with duplicate run ids even though the
   authoritative SOP excludes such batches.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: tests/expected/generated-2.jsonl line 3 contains samples R507-6 and R507-17, both
     with id "R507"; their As counts and internal-standard counts differ (5108.1/46171.1 versus
     11482.8/42686.8). Its expected sample entries require As values 3.5096356342072976 with
     flag "J" and 8.533497448903786 with flag "", respectively. Flip: check_family compares both
     entries. An implementation retaining the shipped report.py’s readings dictionary keyed by
     run id overwrites the earlier reading with the later one; it therefore cannot produce both
     expected values, despite following the SOP for every batch in its declared distinct-id
     domain. The instruction makes the SOP authoritative for that domain, not for this invalid
     batch.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/reduction-sop.md:18-19,
     environment/app/src/metalquant/report.py:13-17, tests/expected/generated-2.jsonl:3,
     tests/test_outputs.py:145-147

3. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR
   The verifier requires a report for a duplicate-run-id capacity batch even though SOP section
   1 expressly requires every run id to be distinct, leaving duplicate-id semantics outside the
   candidate-visible input domain.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: tests/test_outputs.py:219-223 loads and reduces capacity.jsonl. Its sole JSON row
     includes duplicate blank ids, including R458-28 and R458-74 (and also R744-31/R744-77),
     while SOP §1 says every run has a distinct id. Flip: a conforming implementation may
     validate the stated domain and reject this invalid batch, causing the verifier's required
     zero exit assertion at tests/test_outputs.py:115 to fail; another reasonable implementation
     may key readings by id, overwrite one duplicate, and produce a different report. The SOP
     supplies no conflict rule for either behavior, yet the verifier compares the report against
     its private expected value.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/reduction-sop.md:18-20, tests/expected/capacity.jsonl:1,
     tests/test_outputs.py:114-116, tests/test_outputs.py:219-223

4. [Correct Reference Solution] MINOR -- Precision, overflow, and output completeness
   Floating-point response division and intercept cancellation lose the precision needed to
   report an exceptionally small-slope, high-offset calibration accurately.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: Construct a batch with analyte A, mdl=1, loq=5, three standards at concentrations 0,
     500 and 1000, and one sample S with dilution=1. Every is_counts is 1000. Set B=999999000
     and U=2^-23. Standard counts are B, B+5U and B+11U; sample counts are B+7U. These are exact
     terminating decimal JSON numbers (the increments are 0.00000059604644775390625,
     0.00000131130218505859375 and 0.00000083446502685546875). There are no blanks or CCVs. All
     counts and concentrations satisfy section 1. Exact SOP OLS gives slope 11U/1000000 =
     approximately 1.31130218505859375e-12, intercept 999999-U/6000, and sample reading 21500/33
     = 651.515151515..., safely inside the reading range and away from both limits. The correct
     blank level is the retained default 0, so the amount is that reading and the flag is empty.
     In the reference, let q=2^-33, the response ULP near 999999. Dividing the counts by 1000
     rounds the standard responses to 999999 plus 0q, 5q and 11q; the sample response becomes
     999999+7q. The computed mean response is 999999+5q. With mean_x=500, the covariance
     numerator is (-500)(-5q)+(500)(6q)=5500q and the denominator is 500000, giving slope
     0.011q. Subtracting slope*500 from the mean response rounds the intercept to 999999. The
     reported sample reading is consequently approximately 7/0.011=636.363636364.
     Flip: The required numeric comparison changes from passing to failing: the reference
     differs from the SOP amount by approximately 15.151515, versus an allowed error of
     approximately 0.000651515 under instruction.md line 7. Reviewer 1's numerical mechanism is
     confirmed, but this is one defect and its adversarial combination of extremes warrants
     Minor rather than Major. No exclusion in the contract makes the batch invalid; whether this
     precise batch is among the unseen graded files cannot be established.
   Where to look: instruction.md:5-7, environment/app/docs/reduction-sop.md:14-17,
     environment/app/docs/reduction-sop.md:31-41, environment/app/docs/reduction-sop.md:45-55,
     solution/fix.patch:20-32, environment/app/src/metalquant/calib.py:17-19 (+2 more)

novel.explanation: While the editor-state logic in solution/pyed/ed.py mirrors GNU ed's own C algorithm structure (which a model could partially recall), the load-bearing POSIX leftmost-longest regex engine in posixre.py has no analogous reusable reference inside ed's own source (ed delegates regex matching to glibc) and must be independently designed and implemented, preventing a pure memorization shortcut for a significant fraction of the test families.

typos.explanation: No typos found in filenames, paths, commands, or identifiers across instruction.md, task.toml, Dockerfiles, solve.sh, test.sh, or the Python sources (occasional spelling like 'occurences'/'mesages' appears only inside the copied verbatim GNU ed manual text, not in task-authored content).

agentic.explanation: The agent has no ed binary and no network access to obtain one, so it must read the ~1000-line manual (/app/docs/ed.txt), iteratively author and self-test a multi-file implementation, and debug subtle edge cases across many sessions/tool-calls without an oracle to compare against — this cannot be solved by a single zero-shot generation.

solvable.explanation: solution/pyed/ed.py and posixre.py provide a complete, carefully structured implementation (buffer as linked line-nodes, undo stack, active-list global commands, a from-scratch POSIX backtracking regex engine with leftmost-longest semantics) that solve.sh installs into /app/pyed. The code is coherent, internally consistent with the manual's described behavior, and the declared 12-hour expert estimate, while above a 'few hours', is a single workday for an editor+regex-engine port, not a multi-day undertaking.

difficult.explanation: The task requires precise replication of ed's stateful current-address rules, undo-of-undo semantics, global active-list tracking, and, notably, a genuine POSIX leftmost-longest regular-expression matcher, which Python's re module does not provide and which GNU ed itself delegates to glibc rather than implementing — this sub-problem cannot be solved by simply porting ed's own C source and requires real algorithmic/regex-engine expertise.

reviewable.explanation: The verifier derives expected results by executing the actual GNU ed 1.19 binary at test time rather than hardcoding expected outputs, so a non-specialist reviewer can trust the ground truth without ed expertise; task.toml's verification_explanation matches this design precisely.

verifiable.explanation: tests/test_outputs.py runs the real /usr/bin/ed (baked into tests/Dockerfile, root-only after chmod) and the candidate /app/pyed/ed.py against 250+ scripted cases in cases.json, comparing stdout byte-for-byte, exit-status zero-ness, and final directory contents. This is fully programmatic, deterministic (no LLM-as-judge, no randomness), and requires no runtime network installs (pytest/ctrf are pip-installed at image build time in tests/Dockerfile; test.sh only runs pytest).

interesting.explanation: Providing a pure-Python, dependency-free line editor for minimal/distroless container images that still rely on ed-driven maintenance scripts is a real, if niche, systems-engineering scenario (analogous to busybox/toybox utility reimplementations for constrained environments).

binary_reward.explanation: test.sh only ever writes literal `0` or `1` to /logs/verifier/reward.txt on every reachable path (initial default 0, PWD-guard failure 0, pytest success 1, pytest failure 0); no fractional or weighted scoring exists.

task_security.explanation: No credential access, external network calls, obfuscation, or destructive operations were found in environment/Dockerfile, tests/Dockerfile, test.sh, or solve.sh; the 'r /etc/hostname' and 'w ../x.txt' test cases exercise ed's own -r restricted-mode enforcement inside ephemeral tmp directories, not real host paths outside the sandbox.

ctrf_reporting.explanation: test.sh invokes `python3 -m pytest --ctrf /logs/verifier/ctrf.json /tests/test_outputs.py -rA`, emitting a per-test CTRF report covering all 20 discrete test functions to the collected path.

outcome_verified.explanation: Grading is entirely behavioral: stdout bytes, exit status, and resulting files are compared against a live run of real GNU ed; the instruction states the end goal ('behaves exactly like GNU ed 1.19...') and does not prescribe an implementation method beyond a legitimate anti-cheat restriction (stdlib only, no subprocesses).

solution_quality.explanation: solve.sh itself only installs pre-authored files, but the referenced solution/pyed/ed.py (~500 lines) and posixre.py (~200 lines) are genuine, non-trivial, hand-authored implementations kept as separate files rather than heredocs, consistent with the accepted 'write source files that are executed' pattern.

category_and_tags.explanation: category="Software" fits a language/tool-reimplementation task; subcategory="Languages" is a reasonable, defensible fit for reimplementing an interpreter/editor's command language; tags (gnu-ed, line-editor, posix-regex, undo, reimplementation) are specific and directly descriptive of the task's skills.

environment_hygiene.explanation: environment/Dockerfile only COPYs app/ (no tests/ or solution/ leakage, reinforced by environment/.dockerignore excluding both); apt installs in both Dockerfiles are unpinned with proper update+cleanup (`rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*`); test-only pip deps (pytest, pytest-json-ctrf, pinned) live solely in tests/Dockerfile.

no_extraneous_files.explanation: Every file present (instruction.md, task.toml, environment/{Dockerfile,app/*,.dockerignore}, solution/{pyed/*,solve.sh}, tests/{Dockerfile,test.sh,test_outputs.py,cases.json}) is referenced by a Dockerfile COPY, solve.sh, or the test harness; no cruft, backups, or unused assets were found in the full directory listing.

essential_difficulty.explanation: The byte-exact output comparison mirrors ed's actual observable behavior (its own text formatting is the specification, not an arbitrary added format), so difficulty stems from correctly modeling address/undo/regex/global-command semantics rather than from artificial formatting or precision requirements.

anti_cheat_robustness.explanation: The agent's image (environment/Dockerfile) does not install the real 'ed' package and the agent has no runtime network access ([agent].network_mode = "no-network"), so it cannot obtain or shell out to a genuine ed binary to fake correctness. The ground-truth ed binary and all cases.json fixtures live solely in the verifier image, unreachable from the agent container, and are further made root-only before the candidate (demoted to uid 65534) runs.

instruction_concision.explanation: instruction.md is a short, human-sounding narrative (~12 lines), uses absolute paths and backticks for code/paths (`/app/pyed/ed.py`, `/app/docs/ed.txt`), has no headings or roleplay, and describes the required end-state and scope rather than a step-by-step implementation procedure.

do_not_modify_enforced.explanation: instruction.md contains no 'do not modify/preserve/leave unchanged' constraint naming a concrete artifact; it only restricts implementation technique (stdlib-only, no subprocess), which is not a protect-an-artifact constraint.

structured_data_schema.explanation: Output is ed's own raw byte stream (plain text), not a structured data format (JSON/CSV/schema) requiring normative documentation.

functional_verification.explanation: Verification executes both the reference ed binary and the candidate script as subprocesses on real input files and diffs actual stdout/exit-status/file-state; there is no string/keyword matching against source code anywhere in the test suite.

deterministic_reproducible.explanation: pytest==9.1.1 and pytest-json-ctrf==0.5.2 are version-pinned in tests/Dockerfile; the apt-installed 'ed' package is correctly left unpinned per apt conventions; no live external services are used; ed's command scripts and fixtures are static and non-random, so repeated runs should be consistent.

test_instruction_alignment.explanation: cases.json families (addresses, append_insert_change, substitute, global_commands, interactive_global, undo, regex/regex_extended, files_and_write, errors_and_exit, options, odd_files, mixed_scripts_1-8) map directly onto the instruction's enumerated scope; excluded features (-G, -v, h, H, shell '!') were verified absent from the test scripts, matching the instruction's stated exceptions.

separate_verifier_configured.explanation: artifacts=["/app/"] supplies /app/pyed/ed.py to the verifier; tests/Dockerfile pre-installs pytest/pytest-json-ctrf and pre-creates /app and /logs/verifier; no test.sh runtime installs occur; both Dockerfiles pin the identical base-image digest, and no shared assets diverge between environment/ and tests/.

solution_explanation_quality.explanation: solution_explanation accurately summarizes the two-file strategy (posixre.py's exhaustive leftmost-longest matcher, ed.py's linked-list/undo-stack editor model) and is fully congruent with the actual solution/pyed source files inspected.

verifier_execution_isolation.explanation: test.sh chmods /logs/verifier and /tests to 700 (root-only) before any candidate code runs; test_outputs.py executes the candidate exclusively via `setpriv --reuid=65534 --regid=65534 --clear-groups --no-new-privs` (no in-process import of agent code), captures output via communicate() with a 20s timeout and process-group SIGKILL on timeout, and root's test.sh derives the reward solely from pytest's own exit code.

difficulty_explanation_quality.explanation: The explanation concretely names the hard sub-problems (current-address tracking, undo-of-undo, global active-list semantics, interactive G/V, POSIX leftmost-longest regex vs Python's re) and states why an engineer working from memory alone gets specific details wrong; it lacks an explicit one-sentence 'who does this in real life' but the surrounding relevant_experience field and instruction context make this clear by implication.

verification_explanation_quality.explanation: verification_explanation precisely describes the differential-testing strategy (root-run reference ed vs unprivileged candidate, byte-exact stdout/exit-status/file comparisons, root-only ed binary) and matches test_outputs.py and test.sh exactly; no numeric tolerances are used, so no calibration justification is needed.

novel.explanation: While GNU ed's source is public, reproducing its exact behavioral edge cases (POSIX leftmost-longest regex semantics that Python's re lacks, undo-of-undo, global active-list interactions) requires genuine engineering rather than recall of a memorized textbook solution; this is not a standard training-corpus exercise like FizzBuzz or sorting.

typos.explanation: No typos found in task-authored files (instruction.md, task.toml, solve.sh, test.sh, guard.py, test_outputs.py, case files). The single 'occurences' typo found is inside the verbatim upstream GNU ed manual text (environment/app/docs/ed.txt), not task-authored content.

agentic.explanation: The scope (a ~1850-line line editor plus a custom regex engine, validated only indirectly since the agent has no local ed binary or network access to check itself) cannot be produced correctly in a single zero-shot generation; it requires iterative file editing, self-testing, and debugging over many steps.

solvable.explanation: solution/pyed/ed.py and posixre.py provide a complete, structurally faithful port of GNU ed's C implementation (matching known internal function/variable names such as search_line_node, put_sbuf_line, u_current) plus an exhaustive leftmost-longest POSIX regex engine. solve.sh simply installs these pre-written files. Given expert_time_estimate_hours=12 and the size/fidelity of the port, this is achievable by an expert already familiar with ed's algorithm, though it is on the high end of 'a few hours'.

difficult.explanation: Requires precise knowledge of ed's undo/redo semantics, global-active-list bookkeeping, current-address rules after every command, POSIX BRE/ERE leftmost-longest matching (which Python's re does not implement), and error/exit-status edge cases. This goes well beyond a typical undergraduate exercise and matches the stated difficulty_explanation.

reviewable.explanation: Expected outputs are not hardcoded; they are derived at verification time by running the actual GNU ed 1.19 binary, so a non-specialist reviewer can trust the oracle without independently verifying ed semantics. The verification_explanation and difficulty_explanation document the design (roster/fixture self-check, launcher probes) clearly enough for review.

verifiable.explanation: test_outputs.py deterministically runs GNU ed 1.19 (baked into tests/Dockerfile) and the candidate through a launcher, in fresh temp dirs, comparing stdout byte-for-byte, exit status, and resulting files. No LLM-as-judge, no runtime network installs in test.sh (all verifier tooling - pytest, pytest-json-ctrf, ed - is baked into tests/Dockerfile). The roster/fixtures self-check (load_cases) guards against silent corpus drift.

interesting.explanation: Reimplementing a standard POSIX utility for minimal/distroless container images is a realistic professional scenario (embedded/minimal-image maintenance, script portability); the relevant_experience field plausibly identifies the audience (Unix systems engineers maintaining ed/sed scripts).

binary_reward.explanation: test.sh writes exactly 0 initially, then unconditionally overwrites reward.txt with either '1' (rc==0) or '0' (rc!=0) based solely on pytest's exit code; every reachable path writes exactly 0 or 1, with no fractional or weighted scoring anywhere in the verifier.

task_security.explanation: No credential access, no exfiltration, no obfuscation. The guardcheck probes intentionally attempt subprocess/exec/ctypes usage purely to test the anti-cheat guard, which is the guard's own documented purpose. One case reads /etc/hostname via ed's 'r' command, which is benign (compared identically between reference and candidate, no external transmission).

ctrf_reporting.explanation: test.sh invokes pytest with --ctrf /logs/verifier/ctrf.json directly against test_outputs.py, covering its 24 discrete tests (22 case-family tests plus the two guard/package tests), matching the standard CTRF pattern exactly.

outcome_verified.explanation: Tests only check final stdout, exit status, and resulting files against a live GNU ed run; instructions describe required behavior/output, not an implementation approach. No process-level constraints on how the agent must implement pyed.

solution_quality.explanation: solve.sh only copies pre-written solution/pyed/ed.py and posixre.py (each far over 20 lines) rather than inlining them as heredocs, matching the guidance to keep large files separate. The files themselves demonstrate genuine, non-trivial computation (a full editor engine and regex matcher), not a hardcoded answer.

category_and_tags.explanation: category='Software' and subcategory='Languages' reasonably fit a task about implementing a command-language interpreter and its own regex dialect. Tags (gnu-ed, line-editor, posix-regex, undo, reimplementation) are specific and descriptive, not generic.

environment_hygiene.explanation: environment/Dockerfile only COPYs app/ (README, docs, pyed stub); tests/ and solution/ are excluded via .dockerignore and never copied. tests/Dockerfile installs its own test-only deps (ed, pytest, pytest-json-ctrf) at build time, not in test.sh. Apt installs in both Dockerfiles are unpinned (correct per guidance) and followed by rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* cleanup, preceded by apt-get update.

no_extraneous_files.explanation: Every file inspected is referenced by a Dockerfile, the instruction, solve.sh, or the test harness (roster.json/fixtures.json cross-checked against the *.jsonl case files and found perfectly consistent, with fixture and total counts matching exactly). No leftover, backup, or unused files were found; the only hidden file is the standard .dockerignore.

essential_difficulty.explanation: The byte-exact output requirement is intrinsic to faithfully cloning GNU ed's documented behavior (e.g. the 'l' command's escaping rules, diagnostic messages), not an arbitrary formatting overlay bolted onto an otherwise different task. Failures would stem from misunderstanding ed's genuine semantics (current-address rules, undo, leftmost-longest matching), not clerical precision.

anti_cheat_robustness.explanation: The agent image ships no ed binary and has no network at solve time (agent network_mode=no-network), preventing trivial delegation. The guard.py launcher uses sys.addaudithook and a meta_path Warden to block subprocess/exec/fork/ctypes and non-stdlib/non-delivered imports, verified against five probe programs (launcher.py, exec_launcher.py, vendored.py, native.py, plain.py). test_delivered_package_is_standard_library_python additionally scans all delivered files for binary/native content and disallowed imports via AST, closing the loophole of dropping a compiled .so under /app. Ground truth is produced live from the verifier's own root-only /usr/bin/ed, never exposed to the agent.

instruction_concision.explanation: instruction.md is dense but purely descriptive of required behavior (uses absolute paths /app/pyed/ed.py, /app/docs/ed.txt; backticks for commands/paths; no headings, roleplay, or step-by-step procedure). It does not hint at implementation approach (no mention of linked lists, undo stacks, etc.).

do_not_modify_enforced.explanation: instruction.md contains no 'do not modify/preserve/leave unchanged' constraint naming a concrete artifact; its behavioral constraints (stdlib-only, no subprocess, no native code) are enforced by the guard/launcher and delivered-package tests but are not 'do-not-modify-a-file' constraints in the sense this criterion targets.

structured_data_schema.explanation: The task's expected output is plain stdout/file content matching GNU ed's behavior, not a structured schema like JSON/CSV/API response, so no normative schema documentation is needed.

functional_verification.explanation: The core verification (check()) executes both GNU ed and the candidate on 1644 real command scripts and diffs stdout/exit-status/files. The only string/AST-based checks (test_delivered_package_is_standard_library_python) validate the 'stdlib-only, no native code' constraint, which cannot be checked by execution alone and is a legitimate complement, not a substitute, for behavioral testing.

deterministic_reproducible.explanation: Base images pinned by sha256 digest; pytest and pytest-json-ctrf pinned to exact versions; apt-get ed is intentionally left unpinned per guidance (apt mirrors only carry current point releases). No live/mutable network services are used at verify time (network_mode=no-network for both agent and verifier).

test_instruction_alignment.explanation: Every requirement in instruction.md (options -E/-l/-p/-q/-r/-s and no others, address forms, BRE/ERE with GNU escapes, leftmost-longest matching, all other commands/suffixes/global/undo/marks/G/V, error '?' + stop-on-regular-file/continue-on-pipe behavior) is covered by a corresponding case family or the launcher/package tests. Verified absence of excluded features (h/H commands, -G/-v options, '!' usage) in the corpus, matching the instruction's stated exceptions.

separate_verifier_configured.explanation: All verifier inputs (case corpus, guard/guardcheck/guardvendor, GNU ed binary, pytest/ctrf tooling) are baked into tests/Dockerfile; nothing is read from undeclared agent-container paths. No runtime pip/apt installs occur in test.sh. There are no shared assets duplicated between environment/ and tests/ that could drift.

solution_explanation_quality.explanation: solution_explanation accurately describes the two-file approach (posixre.py for BRE/ERE parsing and exhaustive leftmost-longest matching; ed.py for the circular line-list/undo-stack port) and is fully consistent with the actual solution files inspected.

verifier_execution_isolation.explanation: Candidate code always runs via setpriv --reuid=65534 (nobody), never as root, and never in-process inside pytest (always via subprocess.Popen). /logs/verifier and /tests are chmod 700 and the reference ed binary is chmod 700 before any candidate code runs. Reward is derived by root (test.sh) purely from pytest's exit code. The audit-hook guard blocks fork/exec/spawn outright, closing the double-fork-daemon attack this criterion targets; timeouts kill the whole process group via killpg with start_new_session=True.

difficulty_explanation_quality.explanation: difficulty_explanation concretely enumerates the specific hard sub-problems (current-address rules, undo-of-undo, global active-list semantics, interactive G/V, leftmost-longest POSIX matching, error/exit-status nuances) and explains why an engineer working from memory would get specific details wrong. It also clarifies the corpus is synthetically generated from the grammar rather than an external corpus, addressing the data-realism requirement. The real-world audience is covered via the closely related relevant_experience field rather than embedded verbatim in difficulty_explanation, a minor stylistic gap.

verification_explanation_quality.explanation: verification_explanation accurately and specifically describes the verifier's mechanics (roster/fixture self-check, live GNU ed oracle per case, root-only ed binary, unprivileged launcher-wrapped candidate run, byte-for-byte/exit-status/file comparison, five guard probes, delivered-package stdlib/text check), all of which match what was found in test_outputs.py and guard.py.

  [part 1 of 10] The reference is installed at the required path and implements the requested option parsing, alternation direction, leftmost-longest selection, and standard-input reading for interactive globals. Three reachable documented cases nevertheless diverge: setting a filename prints output that `f FILE` must not print; an unmarked address is treated as address zero; and a basic regular expression the manual expressly defines as literal is rejected. The latter can change output, exit status, and whether a file is written.

  [part 2 of 10] The reference distinguishes regular-file and pipe stdin, implements the missing-startup-file branch, and routes command errors through the required stdout notification. Its global substitution loop, however, passes each unconsumed suffix of a line to a new regex search. Word-boundary assertions then see that suffix as the beginning of a word rather than retaining their position in the addressed line. This changes both substitution output and, in some cases, whether a command succeeds.

  [part 3 of 10] The address, option, comment and prompt paths in this part implement their stated rules. A boundary between the join and undo rules does not: a one-line join correctly leaves the buffer unchanged, but discards the undo history of the preceding modification. A subsequent u therefore fails instead of undoing that modification.

  [part 4 of 10] Address offsets, bidirectional searches, empty-pattern reuse and the examined BRE boundaries follow the contract. An unset mark is mishandled specifically in an empty buffer: the reference converts it to address zero, so a command that should fail instead prints a value and exits successfully.

  [part 5 of 10] The reference implements much of the specified regexp and command parsing, but three ordinary, contract-valid regexp boundaries produce different editing results: a leading hyphen in a bracket expression becomes a range, extended-regexp anchors are applied in the middle of expressions, and an interval escape at the start of a basic regexp is rejected rather than matched literally. O85 and O86 describe the same last defect.

  [part 6 of 10] The listed command, suffix, edit, and global-command obligations have corresponding reference paths, including their principal boundary branches. A separate empty-buffer address boundary fails: resolving an unset mark produces the valid append address zero instead of an address error. This changes both output and exit status for a regular-file command script.

Its move-command destination check misses one inclusive boundary: the last line of the moved range is a destination within that range, but the reference accepts it. A short valid pipe-fed script therefore differs in both stdout and exit-success status.

  12. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: Mark management leaves marks attached to detached line
      nodes: substitution fails to transfer a mark to the changed line, and deletion does not

typos.explanation: Spot-checked instruction.md, task.toml, test_outputs.py, guard.py, solve.sh, and case/fixture files for common misspellings and path errors; none were found, and identifiers (family names, fixture keys, file paths) are consistent across roster.json, the .jsonl files, and test_outputs.py.

agentic.explanation: The agent must read the manual and errata, design and iteratively debug a multi-hundred-line editor and regex engine with no reference ed binary available in its own container, requiring exploration, testing, and multi-step iteration rather than a single-shot answer.

solvable.explanation: solution/pyed/ed.py (1426 lines) and posixre.py (333 lines) implement a complete editor model (circular line list, undo stack of add/delete/move records, address parser, POSIX leftmost-longest regex engine) whose comments explicitly track the manual and the errata file, and solve.sh copies them into /app/pyed as the delivered package. expert_time_estimate_hours=12 is on the high end of 'a few hours' but is not a multi-day effort, and a working solution is present.

difficult.explanation: Faithfully reproducing GNU ed 1.19 byte-for-byte requires precise handling of address arithmetic, marks, undo-of-undo, global command active-list semantics, POSIX leftmost-longest BRE/ERE matching (which Python's re does not provide), and manual/implementation divergences — this goes well beyond a standard course project and requires genuine systems/regex-engine expertise.

reviewable.explanation: Expected outputs are derived at verification time by running the real GNU ed 1.19 binary rather than being hardcoded, so a non-specialist reviewer can trust the oracle is 'ed itself' rather than a hand-crafted expected value; the roster/fixture consistency checks make the test corpus auditable.

verifiable.explanation: test.sh runs pytest against test_outputs.py, which for each of 1719 committed cases spawns the image's own /usr/bin/ed (root, as oracle) and the candidate (unprivileged, via guard.py) in fresh directories with LC_ALL=C, and diffs stdout, exit status, and the resulting file tree byte-for-byte. No LLM-as-judge, no network installs at verify time (pytest/ctrf are baked into tests/Dockerfile), and the comparison is fully programmatic and deterministic given GNU ed's own determinism.

interesting.explanation: Porting a POSIX line editor to run in minimal/hardened containers that lack native `ed` (and cannot load native code) is a realistic scenario for engineers maintaining legacy shell/ed-based provisioning scripts in restricted or stdlib-only environments.

binary_reward.explanation: test.sh only ever writes literal `0` or `1` to /logs/verifier/reward.txt, initialized to 0 and set to 1 solely when the root pytest invocation's exit code is exactly 0; no fractional or weighted scoring path exists.

task_security.explanation: Reviewed Dockerfiles, guard.py, test.sh, and all guardcheck probes; no credential access, network exfiltration, obfuscated payloads, or prompt injection was found — probes that spawn subprocesses or load libc exist solely to validate the sandbox guard itself, not to exfiltrate anything.

ctrf_reporting.explanation: test.sh runs `python3 -I -m pytest ... --ctrf /logs/verifier/ctrf.json /tests/test_outputs.py -rA` directly as root, writing the CTRF report to the collected path with full per-test granularity across all 22+ test functions.

outcome_verified.explanation: Grading is purely on final stdout, exit status and resulting files versus the real ed oracle; the only process-level constraints (no subprocess spawn, no native code, stdlib-only) are mechanistic anti-cheat measures explicitly permitted by the rubric, not arbitrary 'use this tool' constraints.

solution_quality.explanation: The reference solution is a genuine, from-scratch implementation of the editor and regex engine (not an echo of expected output), and the large source files are kept as separate files under solution/pyed/ rather than inlined heredocs in solve.sh.

category_and_tags.explanation: category 'Software' fits a from-scratch editor/regex-engine reimplementation; subcategory 'Languages' is a reasonable fit given the command-language parsing and regex-engine implementation work; tags (gnu-ed, line-editor, posix-regex, undo, reimplementation) are specific and directly descriptive rather than generic.

environment_hygiene.explanation: environment/Dockerfile only COPYs app/ (stub ed.py, manual, errata, README) and installs unrelated agent tools (tmux, asciinema, patch, ca-certificates) with apt cleanup; it installs no `ed` binary and no test-only Python packages; tests/Dockerfile owns pytest/ctrf and the real ed binary with its own apt cleanup.

essential_difficulty.explanation: The byte-exact matching requirement mirrors the task's actual goal (drop-in replacement for GNU ed), so precision is intrinsic to the problem rather than incidental formatting noise; failures would stem from genuine semantic gaps (undo, addressing, regex) rather than clerical formatting.

anti_cheat_robustness.explanation: The agent image ships no `ed` binary at all; the verifier's real `ed` is chmod 700 before any candidate code runs; guard.py uses sys.addaudithook/meta_path to block subprocess/exec/fork/ctypes and imports from outside stdlib+delivered files, and this guard is itself exercised against five adversarial probe programs (delegate to ed, exec, ctypes/libc, vendored import, installed package) plus an AST-based audit rejecting delivered executables or foreign imports.

structured_data_schema.explanation: The task's output is plain-text ed stdout and edited text files compared byte-for-byte against the real ed's output — there is no JSON/API/DB structured-output contract requiring a documented schema.

functional_verification.explanation: Correctness is judged by actually executing both the oracle and the candidate program on identical inputs and diffing stdout/exit-status/files; the only source-level scanning (AST import check) exists to enforce the stdlib-only anti-cheat constraint, not as the primary grading mechanism.

deterministic_reproducible.explanation: Both Dockerfiles pin the base image by sha256 digest; pytest/pytest-json-ctrf are version-pinned; apt packages (ed, tmux, etc.) are left unpinned per accepted convention; no live services are used, and LC_ALL=C plus fixed fixtures make ed's behavior deterministic across runs.

test_instruction_alignment.explanation: Every requirement enumerated in instruction.md (options -E/-l/-p/-q/-r/-s, address forms, BRE/ERE with GNU escapes, global/undo/marks/G/V, error/exit-status rules, stdlib-only/no-subprocess constraint) maps to a test family in roster.json or to the launcher/audit tests; no test introduces behavior outside what the instruction and referenced manual/errata describe.

solution_explanation_quality.explanation: solution_explanation accurately describes the two-file port (posixre.py for backtracking leftmost-longest matching, ed.py for the circular line-list/undo-stack editor model) and is fully consistent with the actual solution source files inspected.

verifier_execution_isolation.explanation: The candidate always runs under setpriv as uid 65534 through guard.py, which blocks os.fork/exec/subprocess/ctypes via sys.addaudithook and meta_path before any privileged code path is reachable; /logs/verifier and /tests are chmod 700 and the real ed binary is made root-only before candidate code runs; test.sh (root) derives the reward solely from the root pytest process's exit code, and the guard's own hardening is exercised by dedicated adversarial probe tests (exec_launcher, native ctypes, vendored import, installed package import).

      option and expressly says the task never uses it.
   3. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR: The verifier grades acceptance of -v even though the contract
      explicitly excludes that option and says to implement the six listed options and no
      others.
   4. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR: The contract excludes option -v and says no options beyond its

      equivalence were required.
   5. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR: The verifier requires GNU behavior for the excluded -v option

      enumerated set are required.
   6. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR: The verifier grades the excluded -v option even though the

      excludes it.
   7. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR: The contract expressly excludes the -v option, but the verifier
      grades a -v invocation against GNU ed and therefore silently requires its GNU behavior.
   8. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: The append-command branch never rejects a reversed
      address range, although the erratum reserves acceptance of reversed ranges for `=`.
   9. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: Global substitution rejects only a second encountered
      zero-length match, so it accepts an empty-match-capable expression when its first match
      consumes the whole line.
  10. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: The global-list continuation reader stops at an empty
      continued line and executes the following q as a top-level command rather than as part of
      the list.
  11. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: The regex parser accepts the expressly invalid `\<\>`
      expression as a concatenation of two anchors.
  12. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: An empty line following a backslash-continued
      global-list line prematurely ends list collection, so the subsequent q runs after every
      selected line rather than within the first selected line's list.
  13. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: Global substitution refuses an empty-capable

  14. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: Binary-file state is sticky: after a binary file has

  15. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: The editor never clears isbinary when a later file is

  16. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: Global substitution does not reject a regular

novel.explanation: While GNU ed itself is old and well documented, an exact byte-for-byte clone that also reproduces its 21 documented departures from its own manual, validated against 1770 auto-generated command scripts with live oracle comparison, is not a reproducible-from-memory or easily-copied artifact; a POSIX leftmost-longest regex engine in particular is not something models can shortcut from memorized snippets.

typos.explanation: No typos found in filenames, paths, commands, or variable names across instruction.md, task.toml, guard.py, test_outputs.py, or the solution files during inspection.

agentic.explanation: Requires writing, iterating on, and debugging a large multi-file implementation (editor engine + regex engine) against a wide battery of generated scripts, which cannot be produced correctly in a single zero-shot generation; it demands exploration of the manual/errata and iterative correction against failing cases.

solvable.explanation: A complete reference solution exists (solution/pyed/ed.py, 1426 lines; posixre.py, 333 lines) that ports GNU ed's own C data structures (circular line-node list, undo-atom stack) and implements a POSIX leftmost-longest backtracking regex engine, matching the errata file's documented quirks. The stated expert_time_estimate_hours=12 is on the high end of 'a few hours', but the task is a faithful, scoped transliteration for someone who already knows the ed/regex algorithm, not open-ended research, so it remains within a single expert's working day rather than requiring days of exploratory work.

difficult.explanation: Requires professional-level systems/regex expertise: exact address resolution rules, an undo mechanism that can itself be undone, global-command active-list semantics, and especially a POSIX leftmost-longest regex matcher, which Python's re module cannot express. This goes well beyond an undergraduate course project (a toy ed clone or line-editor assignment would not need byte-exact fidelity to a real program's documented deviations from its own manual).

reviewable.explanation: The canonical GNU ed manual and an explicit errata list (each entry independently checked against the real program) are shipped, and expected outputs are derived live from the real ed binary at grading time rather than hardcoded, letting a non-specialist reviewer trace any test failure back to a documented rule rather than trusting an opaque oracle.

verifiable.explanation: The verifier (tests/test_outputs.py via tests/test.sh) is fully programmatic: for each of 1770 committed cases it runs the real /usr/bin/ed (baked into the verifier image, made root-only before candidate code runs) to get expected output, then runs the candidate under a demoted uid through guard.py, and diffs stdout bytes, exit-zero-ness, and resulting file snapshots. No LLM-as-judge is used. No runtime network installs occur in test.sh (pytest/ctrf/ed are all baked into tests/Dockerfile). This is deterministic and reliable.

interesting.explanation: Grounded in a real scenario: minimal/embedded container images that lack `ed` but still run legacy maintenance scripts (patch/RCS-style ed scripts) piped into it. Systems engineers who maintain such scripts or port CLI tools to minimal images would have genuine use for a faithful pure-Python ed replacement.

binary_reward.explanation: test.sh writes exactly `echo 0` or `echo 1` to /logs/verifier/reward.txt based solely on pytest's exit code (0 or non-zero); there is no intermediate fractional scoring path anywhere in test.sh or test_outputs.py.

task_security.explanation: No malicious code, no credential access, no exfiltration, no obfuscation. The guard/launcher code is a legitimate anti-cheat sandbox, not an attack. A test case reads /etc/hostname via ed's `r` command purely for local output comparison within the same container, not exfiltrated anywhere.

ctrf_reporting.explanation: test.sh runs `python3 -I -m pytest ... --ctrf /logs/verifier/ctrf.json /tests/test_outputs.py -rA`, matching the recommended CTRF pattern directly, with per-test granularity for each of the ~26 pytest test functions plus the anti-cheat and package-audit tests.

outcome_verified.explanation: check() only compares final stdout bytes, exit-zero status, and the resulting directory snapshot — pure end-state comparison. The only process-shaped constraints (stdlib-only, no subprocess/native code) are explicitly stated in the instruction as anti-cheat requirements against trivially delegating to the real ed binary or libc regex, which is the permitted exception for mechanistic anti-cheat constraints.

solution_quality.explanation: solve.sh is a short script that copies pre-written source files into place; the actual computation (the editor and regex engine) is a genuine from-scratch implementation kept in separate files under solution/pyed/, not inlined heredocs, consistent with the guidance for large files.

category_and_tags.explanation: category=Software fits a CLI tool reimplementation task; subcategory=Languages is a defensible if imperfect fit given the heavy parser/interpreter (address grammar, regex engine) nature of the work, though 'Systems'/'CLI Tools' could arguably fit as well or better. Tags (gnu-ed, line-editor, posix-regex, undo, reimplementation) are specific and non-generic.

environment_hygiene.explanation: environment/Dockerfile only COPYs app/ (the stub, manual, errata, README) and installs non-test packages; tests/ and solution/ never enter the agent image. tests/Dockerfile owns all test-only dependencies (pytest, ctrf plugin, ed) baked at build time, not at verify time. Both Dockerfiles follow apt-get update + no cleanup issues (rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*) and leave apt packages unpinned as expected.

no_extraneous_files.explanation: Every file traces to a purpose: environment/app is copied by environment/Dockerfile and referenced by the instruction; tests/cases/*.jsonl and roster/fixtures are loaded and self-validated by test_outputs.py; tests/guardcheck and guardvendor files are all referenced by name in test_outputs.py's guardcheck() test; solution/ files are copied by solve.sh. No leftover or unreferenced files were found.

essential_difficulty.explanation: The exact-byte-match requirement is intrinsic to what a text editor's behavior *is* (its stdout and resulting file state are the whole observable contract), not an arbitrary formatting overlay. The genuine difficulty lies in address/regex/undo/global-command semantics, not in clerical output dressing.

anti_cheat_robustness.explanation: guard.py installs a sys.addaudithook that blocks os.fork/exec/spawn/posix_spawn, subprocess.*, ctypes.*, and imports from outside the stdlib or the candidate's own delivered files, verified against 5 concrete probe programs (delegation, exec, vendored import, native ctypes call, installed-package import) that must all be stopped with status 120. The reference ed binary and /tests are chmod 700 before the candidate ever runs, and the candidate always executes as an unprivileged demoted user (uid 65534). No ground truth is present in the agent image; it only ships a not-implemented stub.

instruction_concision.explanation: The instruction is dense but not padded — no headings, roleplay, or step-by-step procedure; it states the end goal (behave exactly like GNU ed 1.19) and the scope/constraints concisely, using backticks for paths/commands and absolute paths throughout.

do_not_modify_enforced.explanation: The instruction contains no 'do not modify/preserve this artifact' constraint naming a concrete file or object; it only forbids certain implementation techniques (native code, subprocess), which is covered under anti_cheat_robustness, not this criterion.

structured_data_schema.explanation: The task's output is program stdout/exit status/file contents (an editor's ordinary behavior), not a structured data format like JSON/CSV/API schema, so no normative schema documentation is needed.

functional_verification.explanation: Correctness is verified by actually executing both the reference ed and the candidate against 1770 real command scripts and diffing outputs/exit status/files — genuine behavioral testing. A supplementary static AST audit (test_delivered_package_is_standard_library_python) only screens for forbidden native binaries/imports as an anti-cheat backstop; it does not substitute for the primary execution-based grading.

deterministic_reproducible.explanation: Both Dockerfiles pin the exact same base image by sha256 digest; pip packages (pytest, pytest-json-ctrf) are version-pinned; apt packages (ed, tmux, etc.) are left unpinned per accepted convention since apt mirrors only serve current point releases. LC_ALL=C and a fixed minimal env are used for every run, with no network access needed at verify time and no live/mutable external services involved.

test_instruction_alignment.explanation: Every requirement enumerated in the instruction (allowed options, address forms, BRE/ERE with GNU escapes, every command/suffix, global/undo/marks/G/V, error/exit-status behavior, stdlib-only/no-subprocess constraint) maps to a named test family (options, addresses, regex, regex_extended, global_commands, undo, errors_and_exit, files_and_write, plus the launcher/package-audit tests for the stated implementation constraints). No test family checks behavior the instruction doesn't describe.

separate_verifier_configured.explanation: The verifier only reads /app (the declared artifact) plus files baked into the verifier image (/usr/bin/ed, /opt/pyedguard, /tests/cases). All verifier tooling (pytest, pytest-json-ctrf, ed) is baked into tests/Dockerfile; test.sh performs no runtime installs. The two Dockerfiles pin the identical base-image digest, and no shared assets are duplicated between environment/ and tests/ that could silently drift.

solution_explanation_quality.explanation: The solution_explanation accurately describes the two-file design (posixre.py's backtracking leftmost-longest matcher, ed.py's linked-node buffer and undo-atom stack) and is directly congruent with the actual solution/pyed/ed.py and posixre.py source (matching class/field names such as Undo, search_line_node, ustack).

verifier_execution_isolation.explanation: The candidate always runs under setpriv to uid/gid 65534 with --no-new-privs, and /tests and /logs/verifier are chmod 700 before any candidate code executes; root's test.sh derives the reward solely from pytest's exit code, which in turn derives from comparing subprocess return codes/output the demoted child produced. The specific pipe-deadlock risk from a daemonizing grandchild is closed because the audit hook unconditionally blocks os.fork/exec/spawn, preventing the candidate from forking at all.

difficulty_explanation_quality.explanation: The difficulty_explanation is detailed and concrete, naming specific hard sub-problems (address/current-address tracking, undo-of-undo, global active-list semantics, POSIX leftmost-longest matching that Python's re cannot do, error/exit-status edge cases) and explains why an engineer implementing from memory would get them wrong, describing intrinsic difficulty rather than agent pass-rate results. It also states the test corpus is generated (not an external dataset). The 'who would do this in the real world' framing appears in the adjacent relevant_experience field rather than verbatim in difficulty_explanation, a minor placement nit rather than an omission.

verification_explanation_quality.explanation: The verification_explanation precisely matches what guard.py/test_outputs.py implement: live oracle comparison against the image's own ed, root-only sealing of the reference binary, the demoted-user launcher blocking subprocess/native-code/foreign imports, the roster/fixture self-check, and the five guard probes plus the package audit. No unjustified tolerance ranges are used since comparison is exact byte/status/file matching.

1. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR -- Core domain and business logic
   Reading a newline-terminated file after a binary buffer with an unterminated final line
   incorrectly transfers the old line's missing-newline flag to the newly read final line.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: Start with command-line file `original` containing the bytes `a\x00`; supply piped

     reference, `was_bare` is true and `inserted` clears the original tail's flag at lines
     691-695. The read then creates the `b` line with `no_newline=False` at lines 698-714, but
     lines 722-723 set that new last line's flag to true merely because `was_bare` was true.
     Flip: `write_file` lines 744-749 consequently writes `a\x00\nb`, omitting the final newline
     required for the newly read line.

     environment/app/docs/ed-errata.txt:79-84, solution/pyed/ed.py:689-723,

2. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR -- Core domain and business logic
   Reading a newline-terminated file after a binary buffer with an unterminated last line
   incorrectly removes the newline from the newly appended last line.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: Put the three bytes `a\0b` in `original`, the two bytes `c\n` in `second`, and run
     with piped stdin containing `r second\nw output\nQ\n` and FILE `original`. The original
     bare line needs a separating newline when another line is appended; `second` already
     terminates its own line. The contract therefore requires `output` to contain `a\0b\nc\n` (6
     bytes), with a write count of 6. The reference detects `was_bare`, clears the original
     marker at lines 691–695, and reads `c\n` with `no_newline=False` at lines 698–714. But
     lines 720–723 then set the new last line's marker to True solely because `was_bare` was
     True. Flip: `write_file` consequently emits `a\0b\nc` (5 bytes) and prints a write count of
     5.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/ed-errata.txt:79-84, environment/app/docs/ed.txt:942-947,
     solution/pyed/ed.py:689-723, solution/pyed/ed.py:740-754

   A backslash-continued global list stops consuming input at its empty continuation line, so a
   following q executes after all selected lines instead of as part of the list.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: Start with an existing two-line file containing `x\ny\n` and supply `g/./\\\n\nq\n`
     on standard input. The errata explicitly says the empty segment prints each selected line
     twice and the following q belongs to the list. Thus q stops list execution during the first
     selected line: the expected printed lines are `x\nx\n`. The reference assembles only the
     first two script lines into the list, printing `x\nx\ny\ny\n`, then reads q as a top-level

   Where to look: environment/app/docs/ed-errata.txt:67-71, solution/pyed/ed.py:137-159,

4. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR -- core domain and business logic
   Valid long bounded-repeat regular expressions are parsed but matched by unbounded Python
   recursion, causing an unhandled RecursionError instead of GNU ed's successful substitution.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: run with stdin as a pipe containing `a\n` followed by exactly 2,000 ASCII `a` bytes
     and `\n.\ns/a\\{2000\\}/X/\nw out\nq\n`. This is one ASCII text line and uses BRE bounded
     repetition, which the manual defines. The parser accepts the interval (`lo=hi=2000`), then
