agent_result.text_summary:
## Pre-Difficulty Gate Failed

Difficulty not run: the submission did not pass every blocking quality or quality panel check. Oracle/NOP already passed. No Opus, GPT, analysis, or rubric-generation runs were started.

QUALITY PANEL: NEEDS REVISION -- 4 blocking issues to fix. Details for each are below.

Blocking (fix every one):
   1. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR: The verifier requires correct reports for duplicate-ID batches
      that SOP §1 explicitly excludes, silently requiring run-position handling rather than the
      ID-keyed handling sufficient for every contract-valid batch.
   2. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR: The verifier requires distinct results from a batch with
      duplicate run ids even though the authoritative SOP excludes such batches.
   3. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR: The verifier requires a report for a duplicate-run-id capacity
      batch even though SOP section 1 expressly requires every run id to be distinct, leaving
      duplicate-id semantics outside the candidate-visible input domain.
   4. [Correct Reference Solution] MINOR: Floating-point response division and intercept
      cancellation lose the precision needed to report an exceptionally small-slope, high-offset
      calibration accurately.

Checked and clean: Protected Ground Truth, Sound Verifier, Deterministic Execution.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DETAILS
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR -- contradictory input-domain authorities
   The verifier requires correct reports for duplicate-ID batches that SOP §1 explicitly
   excludes, silently requiring run-position handling rather than the ID-keyed handling
   sufficient for every contract-valid batch.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: tests/expected/generated-2.jsonl row 3 contains sample ID R507-6 and a later sample
     ID R507-17, and also repeats CCV ID R124; test_generated_batches loads and compares that
     row. The expected As sample values for the two R507 entries are respectively
     3.5096356342072976 and 8.533497448903786. Flip: an implementation indexing readings by the
     expressly distinct run ID, as the shipped report.py:14-17 does, overwrites the earlier
     reading with the later one and cannot produce both expected values. The complete-report
     comparison at tests/test_outputs.py:125-147 fails, although such indexing is sound
     throughout the SOP's declared distinct-ID domain.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/reduction-sop.md:18-20,
     environment/app/src/metalquant/report.py:13-17, tests/expected/generated-2.jsonl:3,
     tests/test_outputs.py:125-147, tests/test_outputs.py:214-216

2. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR -- contradictory or impossible authorities
   The verifier requires distinct results from a batch with duplicate run ids even though the
   authoritative SOP excludes such batches.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: tests/expected/generated-2.jsonl line 3 contains samples R507-6 and R507-17, both
     with id "R507"; their As counts and internal-standard counts differ (5108.1/46171.1 versus
     11482.8/42686.8). Its expected sample entries require As values 3.5096356342072976 with
     flag "J" and 8.533497448903786 with flag "", respectively. Flip: check_family compares both
     entries. An implementation retaining the shipped report.py’s readings dictionary keyed by
     run id overwrites the earlier reading with the later one; it therefore cannot produce both
     expected values, despite following the SOP for every batch in its declared distinct-id
     domain. The instruction makes the SOP authoritative for that domain, not for this invalid
     batch.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/reduction-sop.md:18-19,
     environment/app/src/metalquant/report.py:13-17, tests/expected/generated-2.jsonl:3,
     tests/test_outputs.py:145-147

3. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR
   The verifier requires a report for a duplicate-run-id capacity batch even though SOP section
   1 expressly requires every run id to be distinct, leaving duplicate-id semantics outside the
   candidate-visible input domain.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: tests/test_outputs.py:219-223 loads and reduces capacity.jsonl. Its sole JSON row
     includes duplicate blank ids, including R458-28 and R458-74 (and also R744-31/R744-77),
     while SOP §1 says every run has a distinct id. Flip: a conforming implementation may
     validate the stated domain and reject this invalid batch, causing the verifier's required
     zero exit assertion at tests/test_outputs.py:115 to fail; another reasonable implementation
     may key readings by id, overwrite one duplicate, and produce a different report. The SOP
     supplies no conflict rule for either behavior, yet the verifier compares the report against
     its private expected value.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/reduction-sop.md:18-20, tests/expected/capacity.jsonl:1,
     tests/test_outputs.py:114-116, tests/test_outputs.py:219-223

4. [Correct Reference Solution] MINOR -- Precision, overflow, and output completeness
   Floating-point response division and intercept cancellation lose the precision needed to
   report an exceptionally small-slope, high-offset calibration accurately.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: Construct a batch with analyte A, mdl=1, loq=5, three standards at concentrations 0,
     500 and 1000, and one sample S with dilution=1. Every is_counts is 1000. Set B=999999000
     and U=2^-23. Standard counts are B, B+5U and B+11U; sample counts are B+7U. These are exact
     terminating decimal JSON numbers (the increments are 0.00000059604644775390625,
     0.00000131130218505859375 and 0.00000083446502685546875). There are no blanks or CCVs. All
     counts and concentrations satisfy section 1. Exact SOP OLS gives slope 11U/1000000 =
     approximately 1.31130218505859375e-12, intercept 999999-U/6000, and sample reading 21500/33
     = 651.515151515..., safely inside the reading range and away from both limits. The correct
     blank level is the retained default 0, so the amount is that reading and the flag is empty.
     In the reference, let q=2^-33, the response ULP near 999999. Dividing the counts by 1000
     rounds the standard responses to 999999 plus 0q, 5q and 11q; the sample response becomes
     999999+7q. The computed mean response is 999999+5q. With mean_x=500, the covariance
     numerator is (-500)(-5q)+(500)(6q)=5500q and the denominator is 500000, giving slope
     0.011q. Subtracting slope*500 from the mean response rounds the intercept to 999999. The
     reported sample reading is consequently approximately 7/0.011=636.363636364.
     Flip: The required numeric comparison changes from passing to failing: the reference
     differs from the SOP amount by approximately 15.151515, versus an allowed error of
     approximately 0.000651515 under instruction.md line 7. Reviewer 1's numerical mechanism is
     confirmed, but this is one defect and its adversarial combination of extremes warrants
     Minor rather than Major. No exclusion in the contract makes the batch invalid; whether this
     precise batch is among the unseen graded files cannot be established.
   Where to look: instruction.md:5-7, environment/app/docs/reduction-sop.md:14-17,
     environment/app/docs/reduction-sop.md:31-41, environment/app/docs/reduction-sop.md:45-55,
     solution/fix.patch:20-32, environment/app/src/metalquant/calib.py:17-19 (+2 more)

novel.explanation: This is a bespoke synthetic ICP-MS batch-reduction codebase and SOP with a custom bug set; it is not a standard textbook exercise or a well-known problem reproducible from memorized training data.

typos.explanation: Targeted search across instruction, SOP, source, tests and solution files found no typos in filenames, paths, commands, or identifiers; cross-references (driver paths, module names, ROSTER filenames/hashes) are consistent.

agentic.explanation: Solving requires reading a multi-section SOP, exploring several interdependent source files (calib.py, blanks.py, samples.py, qc.py, report.py), making coordinated edits, and iteratively verifying against edge cases — this cannot be done in a single zero-shot generation.

solvable.explanation: solution/fix.patch plus solution/solve.sh provides a concrete, self-consistent patch to calib.py, blanks.py, samples.py, qc.py and report.py that implements exactly the five departures described in the SOP (fitted intercept, blank-level mean-of-results, blank-before-dilution amount, corrected-reading flag basis, inclusive-rounded CCV pass, both-sided CCV bracketing, and results-only spike recovery), matching solution/model.py's independent derivation. This is scoped, well-bounded work an expert could complete in a few hours.

difficult.explanation: The task requires precisely translating an 8-section analytical-chemistry SOP into code changes that interact across modules (blank level feeds detection, detection feeds spike eligibility, CCV bracketing feeds every sample/spike), while correctly leaving SOP-silent edge cases (no blank result, one-sided CCV, non-detect spike/parent) untouched. Getting all of the interacting edge cases right without over- or under-fixing is easy to get wrong and requires careful, expert-level reasoning, well beyond a typical undergraduate exercise.

reviewable.explanation: The SOP document, the independently-written model.py (heavily comment-annotated with SOP section references), the patch's section-by-section comment table in solve.sh, and the metadata explanations together let a careful non-specialist reviewer trace every rule from SOP text to code to expected output without needing prior ICP-MS credentials.

verifiable.explanation: The verifier (tests/test_outputs.py) runs the delivered /app/src against a verifier-owned copy of the driver, in a fresh directory each time, as an unprivileged user, and does exact/tolerant numeric comparisons against pre-baked expected reports pinned by SHA-256 in tests/expected/ROSTER. No network calls or LLM judging are used; expected outputs were derived ahead of time from an independent model (solution/model.py) checked in exact rational arithmetic (solution/seal.py). This is deterministic and reliable.

interesting.explanation: Repairing a trace-metal batch data-reduction package to match a laboratory SOP (calibration, blank correction, MDL/LOQ flags, CCV bracketing, matrix-spike QC) is realistic work done by ICP-MS/ICP-OES lab data reviewers under EPA-style methods, as also reflected in the relevant_experience metadata field.

binary_reward.explanation: test.sh only ever writes literal 0 or 1 to /logs/verifier/reward.txt, derived from pytest's exit code (rc -eq 0); no fractional, weighted, or clamped score is ever written.

task_security.explanation: Reviewed environment/Dockerfile, tests/Dockerfile, test.sh, test_outputs.py and solution scripts; no credential access, network exfiltration, obfuscated payloads, or prompt injection. Privilege dropping via setpriv to nobody, process-group kill after runs, and root-only staging directories are all legitimate anti-cheat/isolation code, not malicious.

ctrf_reporting.explanation: test.sh runs pytest with --ctrf /logs/verifier/ctrf.json directly (pytest runs as root here, so no copy-after-run indirection is needed), covering all of test_outputs.py's discrete named tests.

outcome_verified.explanation: Grading is based solely on the JSON report produced by running python3 /app/tools/metalquant_run.py against the agent's /app/src; no particular implementation approach, editor, or step sequence is mandated. The one 'do not modify the driver' constraint is a legitimate, mechanistic anti-cheat/scope constraint, not a procedural instruction.

solution_quality.explanation: solve.sh applies a genuine unified diff (solution/fix.patch) containing real logic changes across five files rather than echoing a final answer; supporting generator/model scripts used to build tests/expected are appropriately kept as separate files rather than inlined.

category_and_tags.explanation: category=Science/subcategory=Chemistry is an accurate fit for an ICP-MS trace-metal data-reduction task, and tags (analytical-chemistry, icp-ms, calibration, blank-correction, quality-control) are specific and directly descriptive of the skills involved.

environment_hygiene.explanation: environment/Dockerfile only COPYs app/ into the agent image, and .dockerignore excludes tests/ and solution/; no test-only or solution-only dependencies are baked into the agent image. tests/Dockerfile owns pytest/ctrf installs and apt is properly update+cleaned where used; apt packages are unpinned as expected.

no_extraneous_files.explanation: Every file inventoried (Dockerfiles, docs, package source, examples, test data/harness, solution scripts/patch) is referenced by a build step, the instruction, the test harness, or the solve script; no cruft, backups, or unused assets were found.

essential_difficulty.explanation: Difficulty stems from correctly reasoning through interacting domain rules (blank correction order, detection-limit gating, CCV bracketing, spike eligibility) rather than from formatting; the numeric tolerance (1e-6 relative/absolute) is generous relative to the exact-arithmetic-checked fixtures, so failures reflect logic errors, not floating-point or formatting minutiae.

anti_cheat_robustness.explanation: Separate-verifier mode keeps tests/expected and solution/ out of the agent image; the verifier records the delivered driver's bytes then swaps in its own copy before every run so a tampered driver can't be used to fabricate output; execution happens as an unprivileged user (uid 65534) with an isolated (-I -S) interpreter from a fresh directory; explicit tests assert the candidate user cannot read tests/expected or /logs/verifier. No ground truth or answer data is reachable from the agent container.

instruction_concision.explanation: instruction.md is dense but purposeful: it states the goal upfront, uses absolute paths throughout (/app/src/metalquant, /app/tools/metalquant_run.py, /app/docs/reduction-sop.md, /app/examples/), contains no roleplay/headings/fluff, and does not hint at which files or functions to change. The detailed range/tolerance enumeration is necessary domain-specific input (comparison rules, section-1 limits) rather than solution hinting.

do_not_modify_enforced.explanation: The instruction's 'leave /app/tools/metalquant_run.py exactly as it is... must still match it byte for byte' constraint is enforced directly: test_driver_is_unchanged compares the driver's bytes captured before verification against the verifier's shipped copy, byte-for-byte. The broader 'add no correction the SOP does not give' behavioral constraint is indirectly enforced by dedicated SOP-silent-case test families that require the shipped (unmodified) calculation to still appear in those specific outputs.

structured_data_schema.explanation: The exact output schema (blank_levels, samples/ccvs/spikes entries with specific keys, list ordering rules, null-vs-number for value) is normatively documented in SOP section 8 (docs/reduction-sop.md), which instruction.md explicitly designates as authoritative, and mirrored precisely by the verifier's ENTRY_KEYS/TOP_KEYS checks.

functional_verification.explanation: The verifier executes the agent's code (via the driver) end-to-end and numerically compares the produced JSON report against independently derived expected values; it does not grep source files or check for keywords.

deterministic_reproducible.explanation: Base images are pinned by digest, pip packages in tests/Dockerfile are version-pinned, apt is not pinned (correct per apt guidance) and has proper update/cleanup. Random batch generation used a fixed seed once, offline, to produce static tests/expected/*.jsonl files that are the only thing read at grading time — no live randomness or external services at verify time.

test_instruction_alignment.explanation: Each named test family (calibration, blank_mean/nondetects/single_result/no_results, dilution, flag_basis/limits, negative_readings, ccv_limits/bracketing/unbracketed, spike_recovery/nondetects, section_one_limits, report_order, generated, capacity, driver-unchanged) corresponds directly to a requirement enumerated in instruction.md/the SOP. The two isolation self-tests (candidate cannot read expected/logs) are harness hardening, not additional agent requirements, and do not contradict the instruction.

separate_verifier_configured.explanation: All verifier inputs (driver bytes, /app/src via subprocess execution) come from the declared artifact (/app/) or are baked into tests/ (shipped driver, expected/, ROSTER); verifier tooling (pytest, pytest-json-ctrf) is pre-installed in tests/Dockerfile with no runtime installs in test.sh; the duplicated driver asset (tests/shipped/tools/metalquant_run.py) is byte-identical to environment/app/tools/metalquant_run.py, confirmed by direct comparison.

solution_explanation_quality.explanation: solution_explanation concisely states the key insight for each of the five fixes and explicitly calls out which SOP-silent behaviors are deliberately left as the shipped calculation; this is fully consistent with fix.patch and model.py.

verifier_execution_isolation.explanation: The verifier's own directories are chmod 700 before any candidate-reachable code executes; the delivered/agent package is only ever run via setpriv as uid 65534 with --clear-groups --no-new-privs, an isolated (-I -S) interpreter, output captured via pipes with process-group kill, and pytest itself never imports agent code in-process (it shells out). Root (test.sh) derives the reward solely from pytest's exit code after the run.

difficulty_explanation_quality.explanation: difficulty_explanation identifies the specific interacting rules that make the task hard, explains why SOP-silent cases are the hardest part, states the data is synthetic but built to resemble real ICP-MS run lists, and names who does this work in practice (an analytical chemist or ICP-MS lab data reviewer) — covering both the human and agent-facing difficulty without citing benchmark/pass-rate numbers.

verification_explanation_quality.explanation: verification_explanation accurately describes the byte-preserving driver swap, unprivileged/isolated execution, exact-match vs. tolerance-based comparison (matching REL/ABS=1e-6 in test_outputs.py), SHA-256/row-count pinning, and the enumerated test families; it states the tolerance values precisely, though it could be marginally more explicit about the rationale for choosing 1e-6 specifically (a generous margin above the internal fixture exactness of 1e-9–1e-12), which is otherwise inferable from solution/seal.py.

   excludes, silently requiring run-position handling rather than the ID-keyed handling
   sufficient for every contract-valid batch.

     row. The expected As sample values for the two R507 entries are respectively
     3.5096356342072976 and 8.533497448903786. Flip: an implementation indexing readings by the
     expressly distinct run ID, as the shipped report.py:14-17 does, overwrites the earlier
     reading with the later one and cannot produce both expected values. The complete-report
     comparison at tests/test_outputs.py:125-147 fails, although such indexing is sound
     throughout the SOP's declared distinct-ID domain.

2. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR -- contradictory or impossible authorities
   The verifier requires distinct results from a batch with duplicate run ids even though the
   authoritative SOP excludes such batches.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: tests/expected/generated-2.jsonl line 3 contains samples R507-6 and R507-17, both
     with id "R507"; their As counts and internal-standard counts differ (5108.1/46171.1 versus
     11482.8/42686.8). Its expected sample entries require As values 3.5096356342072976 with
     flag "J" and 8.533497448903786 with flag "", respectively. Flip: check_family compares both
     entries. An implementation retaining the shipped report.py’s readings dictionary keyed by
     run id overwrites the earlier reading with the later one; it therefore cannot produce both
     expected values, despite following the SOP for every batch in its declared distinct-id
     domain. The instruction makes the SOP authoritative for that domain, not for this invalid
     batch.

     environment/app/src/metalquant/report.py:13-17, tests/expected/generated-2.jsonl:3,

   candidate-visible input domain.

     validate the stated domain and reject this invalid batch, causing the verifier's required
     zero exit assertion at tests/test_outputs.py:115 to fail; another reasonable implementation
     may key readings by id, overwrite one duplicate, and produce a different report. The SOP
     supplies no conflict rule for either behavior, yet the verifier compares the report against
     its private expected value.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/reduction-sop.md:18-20, tests/expected/capacity.jsonl:1,
     tests/test_outputs.py:114-116, tests/test_outputs.py:219-223

4. [Correct Reference Solution] MINOR -- Precision, overflow, and output completeness
   Floating-point response division and intercept cancellation lose the precision needed to
   report an exceptionally small-slope, high-offset calibration accurately.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: Construct a batch with analyte A, mdl=1, loq=5, three standards at concentrations 0,
     500 and 1000, and one sample S with dilution=1. Every is_counts is 1000. Set B=999999000
     and U=2^-23. Standard counts are B, B+5U and B+11U; sample counts are B+7U. These are exact
     terminating decimal JSON numbers (the increments are 0.00000059604644775390625,
     0.00000131130218505859375 and 0.00000083446502685546875). There are no blanks or CCVs. All
     counts and concentrations satisfy section 1. Exact SOP OLS gives slope 11U/1000000 =
     approximately 1.31130218505859375e-12, intercept 999999-U/6000, and sample reading 21500/33
     = 651.515151515..., safely inside the reading range and away from both limits. The correct
     blank level is the retained default 0, so the amount is that reading and the flag is empty.
     In the reference, let q=2^-33, the response ULP near 999999. Dividing the counts by 1000
     rounds the standard responses to 999999 plus 0q, 5q and 11q; the sample response becomes
     999999+7q. The computed mean response is 999999+5q. With mean_x=500, the covariance
     numerator is (-500)(-5q)+(500)(6q)=5500q and the denominator is 500000, giving slope
     0.011q. Subtracting slope*500 from the mean response rounds the intercept to 999999. The
     reported sample reading is consequently approximately 7/0.011=636.363636364.
     Flip: The required numeric comparison changes from passing to failing: the reference
     differs from the SOP amount by approximately 15.151515, versus an allowed error of
     approximately 0.000651515 under instruction.md line 7. Reviewer 1's numerical mechanism is
     confirmed, but this is one defect and its adversarial combination of extremes warrants
     Minor rather than Major. No exclusion in the contract makes the batch invalid; whether this
     precise batch is among the unseen graded files cannot be established.
   Where to look: instruction.md:5-7, environment/app/docs/reduction-sop.md:14-17,

     solution/fix.patch:20-32, environment/app/src/metalquant/calib.py:17-19 (+2 more)

fields.label: Upload terminal bench 3.0 submission here (zip file)

fields.label: Prompt Check
fields.description:
I reviewed my prompt (instruction.md) and:

  • Ensured it does not list an excessive number of requirements (20+)
  • Made it sound natural and human
  • Removed any unnecessary hints and verified it does not reveal the solution
fields.checkboxLabel: I confirm that the above is true and understand that if not, the submission is subject to rejection.

fields.label: Fast static checks
fields.description: Run quick static checks to verify submission structure and files. Submit runs slower checks and agent runs and may take a couple of minutes before returning results.

fields.label: Difficulty check results
fields.description: Please disregard this field if it is blank, during initial submission. This field will be populated by the system when your code is run by the system.

fields.label: Quality Judge Panel Feedback
fields.description:
After initial submission, you will be provided with detailed feedback along 5 axes, each answering a core question about your task:

  1. Coherent Contracts: Can a candidate determine every rule used to grade the task?
  2. Correct Reference Solution: Does the reference satisfy the documented task?
  3. Protected Ground Truth: Can candidate code obtain or control the answer the grader trusts?
  4. Sound Verifier: Does grading reject wrong solutions and accept contract-valid ones?
  5. Deterministic Execution: Does the same submission receive stable grading on repeated runs?

Keep these in mind when reviewing this feedback, and refer to the guidelines for more details on this feedback.

fields.label: Oracle / NOP validation
fields.description: Result of running your reference solution three times and an empty solution once in your task's environment. If your image did not build, the failing Dockerfile step and its output are quoted here. Fix the task, rebuild both images locally on a fresh checkout, and resubmit.

fields.description: This may have duplicate info from above, don't be alarmed. Summary of difficulty check - contains results of agent simulation and stats for each test as well as instruction sufficiency check.
